ModMetadata.Name: ScriptedScreens Vector [StationeersLaunchPad]
ModMetadata.Author: Gruffuss
ModMetadata.Description:
[h1]ScriptedScreens Vector[/h1] [i]Client-side only. Nothing on disk is modified.[/i]
Adds a [b]vector[/b] element type to ScriptedScreens surfaces. Instead of drawing pixel by pixel onto a canvas, you describe a picture once and the game draws it as real geometry — then animates it on your machine, every frame, for free.
[h2]Why you want it[/h2] A canvas console costs roughly [b]10 FPS[/b], and the cause is the number of drawing operations per frame. Every one is recorded, batched, sent over the network, replayed, and uploaded as a texture — sixty times a second.
This makes that count [b]zero[/b]. The scene is sent once. Movement is described with expressions and evaluated on the client, so an animated console needs no per-frame Lua and no per-frame network traffic.
Tessellation runs on a worker thread. A console with 800 shapes animating at 30 Hz costs about [b]0.4% of a frame[/b] on the main thread — a console being switched on is not measurably different from it being off.
[h2]What you can draw[/h2] [list] [*] Rectangles with real rounded corners, ellipses, polygons, SVG paths with holes [*] Smooth liquid surfaces, waveforms and area charts that read as continuous edges [*] Catmull-Rom splines, strokes with caps, joins and dashes [*] Linear and radial gradients, including ones that follow the shape they fill [*] Real alpha — no more pre-composited opaque palettes [*] Antialiased edges, sized in screen pixels so they look right at any distance [*] Convex clipping, so a liquid stays in its tank [*] Opacity ramps along a surface, for gas fades that follow a moving edge [/list]
[h2]How it animates[/h2] Any number can be an expression over [b]t[/b] (time), [b]i[/b] (repeat index) and your own data values:
[code]{ op = "R", x = 10, y = "=100-$fill*100", h = "=$fill*100", f = "#2E8B6E" }[/code]
Send [i]fill[/i] twice a second and the bar moves smoothly at display rate. Values are eased between updates automatically, so a gauge never steps.
[b]hash(i)[/b] gives each instance of a repeat stable pseudo-random values, identical on every client with nothing transmitted — which is what makes a 400-mote particle field cost one node instead of four hundred.
[h2]Resolution independent[/h2] Artwork is written in a viewbox and mapped onto whatever size the element is. The same scene fits a 128 px console and a 760 px one, and stays sharp on both.
[h2]Getting started[/h2] The mod folder contains a numbered set of examples that each run on paste, from a three-shape "hello" up to a complete four-tank gas console, plus a full reference for every node and function.
[h2]Notes[/h2] [list] [*] Text is not drawn by this layer — use ScriptedScreens' own label elements over the artwork [*] Clip shapes must be convex [*] Level of detail is automatic -- update rate and curve smoothness both follow on-screen size; consoles off screen or in a paused game cost nothing [*] Turn on Diagnostics in the settings to see exactly what a scene costs [/list]
[h2]Changelog[/h2] [b]0.7.0[/b] [list] [*] [b]Clickable nodes.[/b] A node marked click=1 becomes a hit region, and the click arrives at the vector element's own on_click with the node id as its value. A list of tappable rows no longer needs a transparent button element over every one of them. [/list] [b]0.6.0[/b] [list] [*] [b]Symbols.[/b] Declare a subtree once with SYM and stamp it with USE, passing parameters — a row, an LED, a duct segment written once and placed twenty times. Substitution happens at parse time, so an instance costs exactly what writing the nodes out would have. [*] [b]Inherited defaults.[/b] A style map on a group or the scene root supplies defaults for everything under it that does not set the key itself. [*] [b]Per-corner radii[/b] on rectangles: rx = { tl, tr, br, bl }, CSS order, and a zero corner is a sharp point. [/list] [b]0.5.0[/b] [list] [*] New [b]T[/b] node: text inside the scene, drawn with TextMeshPro so registered fonts and rich text work. It moves, scales and scrolls with its group like any other node, updates from the data payload with text = "$name", and supports ellipsis and shrink-to-fit. Text was previously label elements laid over the scene, which cost about 300 Lua instructions each, had to be re-declared to change a word, and could not move with the artwork. [*] Strings are now data values, so a data payload can carry text as well as numbers, arrays and colours. [*] Known limit: text clips to an axis-aligned rectangle only. A rounded or rotated clip does not cut it until stencil clipping lands. [/list] [b]0.4.1[/b] [list] [*] Fixed: a fill written as [b]f = "$name"[/b] never worked. The colour was parsed out of the data payload correctly and then dropped before it reached the renderer, so every data-bound fill fell back to white. Colours now arrive like numbers and arrays do. [*] New [b]nodes[/b] prop on the data element: patch any node that carries an id, without resending the scene — nodes = { hv_bar = { w = 42, f = "#E23D3D" } }. [/list]
[b]0.4.0[/b] [list] [*] A scene can now be written as one string in a [b]src[/b] prop instead of nested tables — one node per line, braces for children. A Lua string literal costs zero instructions to build, where nested tables cost about a dozen per node; on a busy console that is the difference between a page fitting in a tick and having to be split across frames. Same ops, keys and expressions as the table form, and it goes through the same parser so the two cannot drift. [/list]
[b]0.3.0[/b] [list] [*] New [b]sh[/b] attribute: CSS box-shadow, several composing in order — { dx, dy, blur, spread, colour }. Drawn as real geometry from the closed form for a blurred edge, so it needs no offscreen pass and no shader. This is the thing feathering could not do: feather ramps outward from a solid edge while a blur softens both sides of it, which is why a feathered knob reads as a ring instead of a shadow. [*] New expression variables [b]sy[/b] and [b]vh[/b] — the scroll offset and viewport height of an enclosing scroll view, in scene units. A vector element inside a scroll view moves with the content; adding sy cancels that out, so a header, fade or rule can stay pinned to the viewport while the content scrolls underneath. Both read 0 when there is no scroll view, so the same scene works either way, and a scene that uses them redraws as you scroll even if it never mentions time. [/list]
[b]0.2.1[/b] [list] [*] The eight worked examples, the authoring guide and the full reference now install with the mod, in the mod's own folder. Previously only the DLL was copied, so there was nothing to read or paste. [*] Fixed: two consoles running the same script fought over one scene registration. Every console names its surface "main", so both hashed to the same key and one console's data reached the other's artwork — seen as clipping breaking on whichever console was started second, and swapping over on restart. Scenes are now keyed per board. [/list]
[b]0.2.0[/b] [list] [*] Tessellation moved to a worker thread. A console with 800 animated shapes at 30 Hz now costs about 0.4% of a frame on the main thread — switching one on is no longer measurably different from switching it off. [*] New [b]fo2[/b] on sampled bands: an opacity ramp along each column, from the sampled edge to the far one. This is how you fade from a surface that moves; a gradient cannot, because it is anchored to the bounding box rather than the wave. [*] Gradients gained [b]units = "bbox"[/b] — a ramp that spans whatever shape references it, and follows that shape when it moves or resizes. [*] Curve level of detail: sampled bands and lines are walked with a longer step when drawn small. Nothing is dropped, the same curve is simply traced with fewer segments. [*] Circles now tessellate by on-screen radius instead of a flat 32 segments, so particles are cheap and large dials are smooth. [*] Shapes that resolve to zero opacity are skipped rather than tessellated, which makes opacity usable as a visibility switch. [*] Clipping no longer allocates per boundary edge, and gained bounds fast paths. Much faster on clipped scenes. [*] Feathering survives a clip and can ramp one edge only ([b]fea_edge[/b]). [*] Clip paths are interpreted in scene coordinates, so a clip keeps clipping the same area however the groups under it are transformed. [*] A scene that draws nothing now shows a magenta hatched border instead of an empty console, with the reason in the log. [/list]
